Calculate age-standardized rate (ASR)

Source: R/create_asr.R
create_asr.Rd

create_asr() calculate age-standardized rates (ASRs) from object with class of canreg, canregs, fbswicd, or fbswicds. It supports stratification by multiple variables, allows the specification of different standard population structures, and provides flexibility in the inclusion of variance, standard errors, confidence intervals, and population data.

Usage

create_asr(
  x,
  ...,
  event = "fbs",
  std = c("cn2000", "wld85"),
  age_breaks = NULL,
  std_method = c("exact", "interpolate"),
  interpolation_method = "linear",
  cancer_type = "big",
  mp = 1e+05,
  decimal = 2,
  show_pop = FALSE,
  show_var = FALSE,
  show_se = FALSE,
  show_ci = FALSE,
  collapse = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'canregs'
create_asr(
  x,
  ...,
  event = "fbs",
  std = c("cn2000", "wld85"),
  age_breaks = NULL,
  std_method = c("exact", "interpolate"),
  interpolation_method = "linear",
  cancer_type = "big",
  mp = 1e+05,
  decimal = 2,
  show_pop = FALSE,
  show_var = FALSE,
  show_se = FALSE,
  show_ci = FALSE,
  collapse = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'canreg'
create_asr(
  x,
  ...,
  event = "fbs",
  std = c("cn2000", "wld85"),
  age_breaks = NULL,
  std_method = c("exact", "interpolate"),
  interpolation_method = "linear",
  cancer_type = "big",
  mp = 1e+05,
  decimal = 2,
  show_pop = FALSE,
  show_var = FALSE,
  show_se = FALSE,
  show_ci = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'fbswicds'
create_asr(
  x,
  ...,
  event = "fbs",
  std = c("cn2000", "wld85"),
  age_breaks = NULL,
  std_method = c("exact", "interpolate"),
  interpolation_method = "linear",
  mp = 1e+05,
  decimal = 2,
  show_pop = FALSE,
  show_var = FALSE,
  show_se = FALSE,
  show_ci = FALSE,
  collapse = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'fbswicd'
create_asr(
  x,
  ...,
  event = "fbs",
  std = c("cn2000", "wld85"),
  age_breaks = NULL,
  std_method = c("exact", "interpolate"),
  interpolation_method = "linear",
  mp = 1e+05,
  decimal = 2,
  show_pop = FALSE,
  show_var = FALSE,
  show_se = FALSE,
  show_ci = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

The input data, object with class of 'fbswicd', 'fbswicds', 'canreg', or 'canregs'.

...

One or more variables used for stratification. For example, you can stratify by sex, year, cancer, or just by year. If sex is not passed as a parameter, the output will be the result for the combined gender.

event

A variable used to specify the type of calculation, options are "fbs" or "sws", "fbs" for cancer incidence, and "sws" for cancer mortality.

std

Specify the standard population structure in the 'std_pop' data frame used for calculating standardized rates. When calculating standardized rates for multiple standard populations, specify std = c(segi, china).

age_breaks

Numeric vector of lower bounds for input age groups. It must begin at 0 and end no later than 85. The final group is open-ended. If omitted, the bounds are inferred from agegrp.

std_method

Method used to align standard-population weights with age_breaks: "exact" combines original groups, while "interpolate" estimates single-year weights before regrouping.

interpolation_method

Interpolation method used when std_method = "interpolate".

cancer_type

A character string specifying the classification method used to categorize ICD-10 codes. This determines how ICD-10 codes are classified. Options include "big" (classify ICD-10 codes into 26 cancer categories), "small" (classify ICD-10 codes into 59 cancer categories, more specific categories), "system" (classify ICD-10 codes into organ system), and "gco" (classify ICD-10 code into cancer categories same as classification published by the Global Cancer Observatory), and "ci5" (classify ICD-10 codes using the 63-category CI5-XII classification, with shared aggregate codes 60 and 61). This parameter is only available when the input data is a vector of ICD-10 codes, or object with class of 'canreg' or 'canregs'.

mp

A constant to multiply rates by (e.g. mp=1000 for rates per 1000).

decimal

This parameter specifies the number of decimal places to round the results. The default is 2, which means rates will be rounded to two decimal places.

show_pop

Logical value whether output population or not.

show_var

Logical value indicating whether to output variances. Variances use the squared scale of the reported rates, so their square roots equal the corresponding standard errors before rounding.

show_se

Logical value indicating whether to output standard errors. Standard errors use the same scale as the reported rates.

show_ci

Logical value whether output confidence(lower or upper bound) or not.

collapse

Logical value whether output result as asr or asrs.

Value

A data frame or tibble contains the age standard rates and CIs.

Details

Standard populations use 19 age groups by default: age 0, 1–4, 5–9, ..., and 85+. When the input uses 18 five-year age groups beginning with 0–4, create_asr() automatically combines the age-0 and age-1–4 standard-population weights before calculating the ASR.

Supply age_breaks to use another compatible grouping. By default, groups must only combine the original standard-population groups; set std_method = "interpolate" when a requested boundary splits one.

For summary input, existing sex = "0" rows are retained once. Missing overall rows are computed from available male/female rows at each original stratum before grouping. If an overall row and both sex-specific rows are supplied, inconsistent totals cause an error. Overall-only input is supported; sex-specific rows are not inferred from overall values. Within each observed year/sex/cancer stratum, absent summary age rows are interpreted as zero counts and completed from matching population age groups. Entirely absent strata are not inferred. Supplied missing, non-finite, or negative counts cause an error; population rows are never invented or filled with zero.

See also

ageadjust for age-adjusted rate calculations. truncrate for truncated rate calculations.

Examples

data("canregs")
asr_inci <- create_asr(canregs, event = "fbs", year, sex, cancer)
asr_mort <- create_asr(canregs, event = "sws", year, sex, cancer)

# calculate ASR based on object with class of `canregs`
asr <- create_asr(canregs, event = "sws", year, sex, cancer)

# calculate ASR based on object with class of `canreg`
data <- canregs[[1]]
# calculate ASR using default parameter
asr <- create_asr(data, year, sex, cancer)
head(asr)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 12
#>   year  sex   cancer no_cases    cr asr_cn2000 asr_wld85 truncr_cn2000
#>   <chr> <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 2021  0     101          38  5.53       3.74      3.79          5.6 
#> 2 2021  0     102           5  0.73       0.71      0.71          1.29
#> 3 2021  0     103          59  8.58       4.53      4.85          6.13
#> 4 2021  0     104         123 17.9       11.1      11.2          13.7 
#> 5 2021  0     105         236 34.3       20.6      20.2          28.4 
#> 6 2021  0     106         128 18.6       11.5      11.4          17.1 
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: truncr_wld85 <dbl>, cumur <dbl>, prop <dbl>, rank <int>
# calculate ASR using multiple standard population
asr_multi_std <- create_asr(data, year, sex, cancer,
  std = c("cn82", "cn2000", "wld85")
)
head(asr_multi_std)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 14
#>   year  sex   cancer no_cases    cr asr_cn82 asr_cn2000 asr_wld85 truncr_cn82
#>   <chr> <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 2021  0     101          38  5.53     3.07       3.74      3.79        6.14
#> 2 2021  0     102           5  0.73     0.74       0.71      0.71        1.32
#> 3 2021  0     103          59  8.58     3.26       4.53      4.85        6.85
#> 4 2021  0     104         123 17.9      8.33      11.1      11.2        15.0 
#> 5 2021  0     105         236 34.3     14.9       20.6      20.2        30.5 
#> 6 2021  0     106         128 18.6      8.6       11.5      11.4        18.4 
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: truncr_cn2000 <dbl>, truncr_wld85 <dbl>, cumur <dbl>,
#> #   prop <dbl>, rank <int>
# calculate ASR with confidence interval
asr_with_ci <- create_asr(data, year, sex, cancer, show_ci = TRUE)
head(asr_with_ci)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 18
#>   year  sex   cancer no_cases    cr cr_lower cr_upper asr_cn2000
#>   <chr> <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 2021  0     101          38  5.53     3.91     7.59       3.74
#> 2 2021  0     102           5  0.73     0.24     1.7        0.71
#> 3 2021  0     103          59  8.58     6.53    11.1        4.53
#> 4 2021  0     104         123 17.9     14.9     21.4       11.1 
#> 5 2021  0     105         236 34.3     30.1     39.0       20.6 
#> 6 2021  0     106         128 18.6     15.5     22.1       11.5 
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: asr_lower_cn2000 <dbl>, asr_upper_cn2000 <dbl>,
#> #   asr_wld85 <dbl>, asr_lower_wld85 <dbl>, asr_upper_wld85 <dbl>,
#> #   truncr_cn2000 <dbl>, truncr_wld85 <dbl>, cumur <dbl>, prop <dbl>,
#> #   rank <int>
# calculate ASR with population at risk
asr_with_pop <- create_asr(data, year, sex, cancer, show_pop = TRUE)
head((asr_with_pop))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 13
#>   year  sex   cancer    pop no_cases    cr asr_cn2000 asr_wld85 truncr_cn2000
#>   <chr> <chr> <chr>   <int>    <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 2021  0     101    687356       38  5.53       3.74      3.79          5.6 
#> 2 2021  0     102    687356        5  0.73       0.71      0.71          1.29
#> 3 2021  0     103    687356       59  8.58       4.53      4.85          6.13
#> 4 2021  0     104    687356      123 17.9       11.1      11.2          13.7 
#> 5 2021  0     105    687356      236 34.3       20.6      20.2          28.4 
#> 6 2021  0     106    687356      128 18.6       11.5      11.4          17.1 
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: truncr_wld85 <dbl>, cumur <dbl>, prop <dbl>, rank <int>
# calculate ASR with standard errors
asr_with_se <- create_asr(data, year, sex, cancer, show_se = TRUE)
head(asr_with_se)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 15
#>   year  sex   cancer no_cases    cr cr_se asr_cn2000 asr_se_cn2000 asr_wld85
#>   <chr> <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 2021  0     101          38  5.53  0.9        3.74          0.68      3.79
#> 2 2021  0     102           5  0.73  0.33       0.71          0.35      0.71
#> 3 2021  0     103          59  8.58  1.12       4.53          0.63      4.85
#> 4 2021  0     104         123 17.9   1.61      11.1           1.08     11.2 
#> 5 2021  0     105         236 34.3   2.23      20.6           1.41     20.2 
#> 6 2021  0     106         128 18.6   1.65      11.5           1.07     11.4

#> #   truncr_wld85 <dbl>, cumur <dbl>, prop <dbl>, rank <int>

# calculate ASR based on object with class of `fbswicds`
# convert object with class of `canregs` to object with class of `fbswicds`
fbsws <- count_canreg(canregs)
asrs <- create_asr(fbsws, event = "sws", year, sex, cancer)

# calculate ASR based on object with class of `fbswicd`
# convert object with class of `canreg` to object with class of `fbswicd`
fbsw <- count_canreg(canregs[[1]])
asr <- create_asr(fbsw, event = "sws", year, sex, cancer)
